name: Indigenous feminism
summary: Indigenous feminism treats colonisation as the source of the imposed patriarchy and heteronormativity that subordinate Indigenous women, and makes decolonisation, land and Indigenous self-determination the centre of gender justice. It is intersectional and collectivist, preferring responsibility and relation to Western liberal individualism, and gives priority to ending violence against Indigenous women. Its thinkers insist that self-government must include women and gender-diverse people rather than replicate settler or male-dominated state forms.
scope: The Indigenous feminism of North America, with some reference to Sapmi, Australia and Mexico, as in Joyce Green's collection Making Space for Indigenous Feminism, Andrea Smith's 'Indigenous Feminism Without Apology', Rauna Kuokkanen's work on self-determination and gender, and the Canadian national inquiry into missing and murdered Indigenous women. Economic, foreign-policy and institutional-design answers are mostly low-confidence inferences from its anticolonial, anti-capitalist and anti-hierarchy commitments; some Indigenous women reject the feminist label, and strands differ on sex work, abolition and the role of the state.

keyFigures.name: Rauna Kuokkanen
keyFigures.role: Sami scholar who argues Indigenous self-determination must restructure gendered relations of domination.

keyFigures.name: Aileen Moreton-Robinson
keyFigures.role: Aboriginal Australian scholar cited in the Wikipedia article for her view of Indigenous women's shared experience of exclusion.

sources.title: Indigenous feminism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, regional strands, colonialism, patriarchy, land, capitalism, reproduction, MMIW and debates.

sources.title: Indigenous Feminism Without Apology
sources.author: Andrea Smith
sources.usedFor: Sovereignty beyond the nation-state, heteropatriarchy and empire, non-hierarchical governance, violence against Native women.

sources.title: Review of Restructuring Relations: Indigenous Self-Determination, Governance, and Gender
sources.author: Joyce Green, Canadian Journal of Political Science
sources.usedFor: Kuokkanen's argument on land, self-determination, gendering self-government and treaties.

sources.title: Reclaiming Power and Place: executive summary of the Final Report of the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls
sources.author: National Inquiry into MMIWG (via YouthREX)
sources.usedFor: Colonial and patriarchal roots of violence, rights violations, poverty and marginalisation, transformative change.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The inquiry's testimony names barriers to health care as part of Indigenous women's marginalisation, so a state guarantee fits, though the sources do not discuss universal systems.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wikipedia describes poverty and economic exclusion of Indigenous women, which suggests support for wage floors; the minimum wage itself is not discussed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Indigenous feminism treats settler capitalism and private property as colonial impositions that undermined women's economic authority, so market superiority is doubtful.

public-ownership.rationale: Land and resources are claimed as Indigenous commons, not state property, so adherents would not simply endorse nationalised utilities; no source addresses this.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Concern with poverty and the economic legacy of colonisation points to redistribution, though taxation is not a topic in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: Collectivist, anti-exploitation commitments suggest sympathy for unions; the sources do not discuss unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wikipedia says settlers imposed private property and capitalist economies that disrupted Indigenous women's economic authority, so property rights as an overriding value are rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The inquiry links resource extraction camps and industry to violence against Indigenous women, which supports tighter control of corporations; this is inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Poverty and housing insecurity are cited as drivers of violence against Indigenous women, so cutting welfare runs against their analysis.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership resonates with communal values but the sources say nothing about worker-owned firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Smith's critique of state domination and coercion implies distrust of expanded state surveillance; surveillance is not discussed directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The sources do not address drug policy; Indigenous communities are divided on it given addiction harms and criminalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose racist and sexist abuse but are wary of state criminal law, so they split.

strong-leader.rationale: Smith's vision of sovereignty built on interrelatedness and non-hierarchy rejects strongman rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Smith says sovereignty is not an add-on to the nation-state and calls for separating liberation from state-building, yet most adherents still demand state accountability and treaty rights.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; adherents are divided between safety concerns and hunting and treaty rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: The inquiry documents police failures toward Indigenous women, so more police power is unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Indigenous feminists are split, with some seeing sexual exploitation of Indigenous women as colonial violence and others supporting decriminalisation; the sources do not decide it.

decide-locally.rationale: Self-determination and community-level governance are core, though Smith warns against simply replicating nation-state forms.

rehabilitation.rationale: The inquiry calls for transformative justice responses and cites the over-criminalisation of Indigenous people; rehabilitation over punishment is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Wikipedia reports that colonial authorities imposed monogamy, domesticity and patriarchal family norms, which Indigenous feminists reject; kinship is valued but not the imposed nuclear model.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Smith criticises the Navajo same-sex marriage ban and heteronormative nationalisms, so legal recognition is supported.

abortion-legal.rationale: Wikipedia covers forced sterilisation as colonial control of Indigenous women's bodies, implying bodily autonomy, but abortion itself is not discussed and views vary.

more-religion-public.rationale: Missionaries are described as agents of colonial gender norms; Indigenous spirituality is valued but a larger public role for religion is not endorsed. Inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The inquiry calls for transformative legal and social change to address deliberate rights violations, and decolonisation is the central aim of the movement.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Wikipedia says colonisers reshaped Indigenous gender expression and sexuality, implying gender norms are socially made, though many stress Indigenous understandings of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Indigenous cultural preservation is central, but this statement refers to a national culture of the settler state, which adherents do not champion; read literally it is split.

gradual-change.rationale: Smith's decolonial politics demands structural transformation rather than gradual reform within established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; adherents stress that settler states are themselves colonial, and generally oppose anti-immigrant politics.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Indigenous movements use the UN and international law to assert rights, but sources do not discuss empowering such bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Wikipedia notes harm from capitalist restructuring (for example neoliberal restructuring in Oaxaca) to Indigenous women.

nation-first.rationale: Smith separates liberation from nation-state building and criticises nationalism as heteropatriarchal.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Smith links patriarchy to empire building, so adherents distrust military intervention; not directly discussed.

open-borders.rationale: Smith critiques "we're American too" claims as legitimising colonisation, but this does not translate into a clear border position.

limit-growth.rationale: Wikipedia describes Indigenous environmental care as reciprocal responsibility among humans, non-humans and land, in tension with endless growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Wikipedia notes climate change harms Indigenous women's food security, and the tradition frames care for land as a duty, but no source calls for drastic action by the settler state, of which Smith is wary; this is an inference.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Land-based, relational knowledge is prized over techno-solutionism; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Reciprocal responsibility to land and Indigenous communities' experience of uranium mining suggest opposition; not discussed in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Smith centres anticolonial resistance since 1492 and calls for transformation of the state system, though the sources do not discuss revolution as such.

experts-over-public.rationale: Kuokkanen argues Indigenous women's own views must be central rather than overridden by outside or elite frameworks.

central-planning.rationale: Anti-hierarchy and anti-domination themes cut against central planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources do not consider market forms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; Indigenous land is not conceived as taxable property.

basic-income.rationale: Poverty is named as a driver of vulnerability, so income security is plausible; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Private property is described as a colonial imposition; communal land holding is preferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not addressed; critique of capitalism is not a call to abolish wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the movement's economic critique targets colonial extraction, not monetary institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised peak bodies fit poorly with Smith's non-hierarchical, anti-state-domination stance; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Smith rejects domination and hierarchy as organising principles, so a single guiding party is incompatible.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Smith's critique of hierarchy implies rejecting hereditary rule; Indigenous hereditary systems are a distinct matter and not addressed.

democracy-best.rationale: Kuokkanen wants participatory, gendered self-government, but she and Smith criticise settler-state democracy as colonial; the sources do not give a verdict.

direct-votes.rationale: Participatory themes fit but consensus-based Indigenous decision-making is not the same as referendums; not addressed.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is not organised around class councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Kuokkanen and Smith treat Indigenous self-determination as a right that may go beyond settler-state sovereignty, though secession is rarely the stated goal.

natural-rulers.rationale: Smith says pre-colonial Native communities were not structured by hierarchy and calls for non-domination.

political-violence-never.rationale: Smith honours anticolonial resistance since 1492; the sources do not endorse violence but do not rule out resistance.

war-builds-character.rationale: Smith links militarism to patriarchy and empire; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split because Indigenous spirituality is bound up with governance.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Missionary and Christian impositions on Indigenous gender relations are criticised; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Privatised coercion conflicts with Smith's anti-domination politics; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Smith separates national liberation from nation-state building and criticises exclusionary nationalisms.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Colonialism, not class, is the main frame in the sources.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek restoration of rights and power more than outcome equality as such.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Kuokkanen says Indigenous feminism places self-determination and the question of land at the heart of its theory and activism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The inquiry frames the violence as rooted in rights violations that require transformative redress; reparations specifically are not discussed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Kim Anderson and Wikipedia contrast Indigenous responsibility-based collectivism with Western liberal individualism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kim Anderson favours responsibility-based over rights-based approaches, but Kuokkanen and Smith defend women's rights within communities, so adherents are split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Wikipedia describes care for land as reciprocal responsibility among humans, non-human beings and land.

limit-population.rationale: State control of Indigenous reproduction, including sterilisation, is documented as colonial violence.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Land loss and environmental harm are tied to settler industrialism; the sweeping claim is inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Disruption to Indigenous communities by outside change is a concern; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources never discuss body modification technology; adherents' concern with bodily autonomy and with state control of bodies pulls both ways.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Relational, women-inclusive self-government is the model; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: None of the sources touch encryption; distrust of state surveillance of Indigenous communities is offset by no stated position on tools.

restore-past-order.rationale: Smith says communities will not recreate past forms but pre-colonial arrangements show alternatives, so restoration is not the aim as stated.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; decolonial principle guides policy.

direct-action.rationale: Wikipedia describes activism such as Idle No More, vigils and grassroots advocacy alongside engagement with institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Smith says sovereignty should be predicated on interrelatedness and responsibility rather than domination, so methods should model the aim.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not advocated; land-based practice is valued but not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; the critique is of colonial gendered labour roles.

production-for-use.rationale: Land-based, reciprocal economies are preferred to colonial capitalism; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed in classic Marxist terms.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial rule conflicts with Smith's stance against domination.

collective-farming.rationale: Communal land stewardship is valued in the sources, but nothing says farming should be organised collectively rather than by families or nations.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Smith links empire to patriarchy rather than to capitalism by necessity.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; colonial state taxation may be contested but libertarian framing is foreign to the movement.

harm-principle.rationale: The sources take no stand on liberal limits on state power; the movement's focus is on colonial harms rather than on a general principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Wikipedia reports Indigenous feminism is collective and, per Kim Anderson, favours responsibility-based collectivism over Western liberal rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Land-based peoples cannot simply exit; Kuokkanen stresses voice and participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Market logic is criticised as colonial; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Kuokkanen's integrity norm and the movement's attention to material conditions fit a substantive view of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; academic co-optation is a concern in Wikipedia, but the claim is not endorsed.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The framework rests on colonial structures, not biology, and rejects racist hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Community-based representation fits, but the corporatist form is not endorsed.

total-state.rationale: Smith rejects domination and coercion by the state.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Colonial territorial expansion is the central wrong the ideology addresses.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Hierarchy and lordship are opposed; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Wikipedia and Kuokkanen say mainstream and academic frameworks side-line Indigenous women's knowledge, and that knowledge frameworks reflect power.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement rejects Western universal frameworks imposed on Indigenous communities, favouring Indigenous paradigms; some defend universal human rights, so split lean.

single-common-good.rationale: Kuokkanen demands attention to women's views that single frameworks have brushed aside.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; Indigenous feminists are divided and generally critical of settler states.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources discuss peoples rooted in their own lands, not a general right of return for diasporas to a nation-state.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cultural and language losses and state denial of Indigenous identities are named as core harms.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Participatory, inclusive governance fits; not addressed for firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: The sources never mention school funding models; the concern in them is Indigenous control of education and language, which vouchers do not directly address.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed; poverty concerns suggest tolerance of spending, but nothing in the sources states it.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic liberalism is tied to settler capitalism in Wikipedia's account.

rule-by-example.rationale: The sources do not address moral example versus law as a basis of rule; relational governance ideals are not framed this way.

national-self-determination.rationale: Kuokkanen centres Indigenous self-determination, but Smith explicitly rejects tying sovereignty to the nation-state, so the statement's 'in its own state' is resisted; this is an inference from both.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Indigenous knowledge and spirituality are valued.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; adherents emphasise that settler citizenship itself is contested, and oppose anti-immigrant policy.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Structural poverty is cited as the cause of harm; conditionality is likely rejected.

class-collaboration.rationale: The sources frame conflict as colonial rather than between classes, so employer-worker partnership is not addressed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural continuity is a central concern; destroying heritage runs against it.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; national framing is criticised by Smith.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Wikipedia reports colonisers imposed gender roles and patriarchy, and Indigenous women claim roles in governance.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is not discussed anywhere in the sources.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racialised legal separation such as the Indian Act regime is criticised as colonial discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Smith frames the state as a tool of colonial and heteropatriarchal domination, not strictly class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The inquiry links extractive industry to violence against Indigenous women, and Wikipedia covers climate harm to Indigenous women.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Assimilationism echoes colonial policy that the movement criticises; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claims conflict with its anti-racist politics.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources; Kuokkanen's concern is Indigenous women's inclusion in governance, not the settler voting formula.

national-mission.rationale: Smith ties national missions to empire.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wikipedia says colonisation imposed patriarchal systems that subordinated women, and Indigenous feminism opposes heteropatriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed; Kuokkanen criticises male-dominant elites in Indigenous governments, but a general claim is not stated.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Wikipedia documents eugenics boards that sterilised Indigenous women as colonial violence.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The inquiry calls for accountability for institutional failures and rights violations and finds laws and institutions perpetuate them.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement demands state action on MMIW, poverty and rights restoration.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Regulation of Indigenous intimate life is condemned as colonial.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal rights and human rights for Indigenous women are core aims.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that the sources do not touch.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Wikipedia says settler colonialism works through land appropriation and regulation of Indigenous gender and kinship.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Kuokkanen supports Indigenous self-government with its own governance, implying plural legal orders, though women's equality is to be entrenched.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; colonial missionary conversion is criticised.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A question from South Asian politics that the sources do not address; Indigenous hunting and food practices argue against blanket bans on animal use.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Residential school and missionary education are part of colonial history; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A debate internal to Soviet-era socialism that the sources do not address.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kuokkanen argues Indigenous peoples' own consent and self-determination, including women's, underlie legitimate governance; settler states lacking it are criticised.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals are not discussed in the sources.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of Indigenous peoples is part of the colonial history the ideology opposes.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed in the libertarian sense; state violence is opposed but resistance is honoured.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Collectivist, relational values are preferred over competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are not discussed; adherents distrust state coercion but also oppose racist movements.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Kuokkanen describes self-determination as seeking to restructure all relations of domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; Kuokkanen argues for gendering institutions generally.

vanguard-party.rationale: Smith rejects hierarchy and domination in organising; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The inquiry places poverty, housing insecurity and marginalisation at the root of vulnerability to violence.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are not discussed; housing insecurity is named as a harm but the tenure question is not.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is attributed to colonial dispossession.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement opposes racist claims and sees colonial hierarchy as the source of conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in the sources, though participatory ideals might sympathise.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; food security is a concern but price-fixing policy is not mentioned.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Immigration and citizenship rules are not discussed; Smith rejects settler claims to belonging but offers no rule for naturalisation.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; anti-hierarchy ideals could favour it but there is no statement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not discussed in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Kuokkanen criticises settler sovereignty but pooling is not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrated command conflicts with non-domination; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Heteropatriarchal religious authority is criticised for excluding women.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a debate within Marxism that the sources do not address.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship conflicts with anti-coercion politics; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Accountability of leaders to communities fits; not addressed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not discussed in the sources.

people-in-arms.rationale: Citizen militias are not discussed; Smith's distrust of state militarism is balanced by Indigenous traditions of self-defence not covered in the sources.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Land connection is valued, but urban Indigenous women are a major part of the movement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Wikipedia and Kuokkanen note peoples divided by colonial borders (Sami across states, Indigenous peoples across Canada and the United States); inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is strongly academic.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The movement rejects hierarchies of civilisation, though it also criticises patriarchal practice within communities.

death-penalty.rationale: State punishment falls disproportionately on Indigenous people; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed directly; gender equality education fits the movement's aims.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Indigenous creation teachings are valued but separate from Christian creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; sexual commodification of Indigenous women is criticised, but adherents differ on legal restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Wikipedia covers the Indian Act's patrilineal status rules as discriminatory, but this statement concerns state citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Cultural and language losses and state denial of identity are named as core harms to be reversed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Protection of Indigenous spiritual practice is plausible; not addressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument about conformity is not discussed; Indigenous feminism criticises imposed norms but also stresses collective belonging.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Wikipedia links settler capitalist economies to the disruption of Indigenous women's economic authority, so decolonisation includes economic change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; Kuokkanen wants gendered treaty and self-government negotiations.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-extractive stance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional design of the presidency is not discussed in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary policy governance is not discussed in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Land is central to the movement, but the statement concerns interstate peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property is seen as a colonial imposition and land as held in responsibility.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist historical debate the sources do not address.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Responsibility to land and future generations underlies Indigenous environmental ethics in Wikipedia.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance obligations are not discussed; Smith's anti-imperial stance suggests distrust but the sources do not state it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Territory taken without consent is the core grievance of settler colonialism; applying to annexation is inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; state domination of Indigenous institutions is opposed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss the role of heads of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Opposed to coercive imposition of settler sovereignty; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Kuokkanen supports self-government with distinct legal and political orders within states; the Zapatista autonomy won constitutional recognition (Wikipedia).

character-from-environment.rationale: Gender and character are shaped by colonial structures in Wikipedia's account.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Smith rejects domination and unaccountable power.

space-expansion.rationale: Relationship to land and Earth is central; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed in the sources.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules are not discussed; kinship and responsibility matter, but no presumption of equal time is stated.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Maoist theory that the sources do not address.

land-redistribution.rationale: Return of land to Indigenous communities is central, though this statement concerns estates redistributed to farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Return to land and community after displacement fits the movement's aims; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Wikipedia reports that colonial authorities enforced modesty and domesticity on Indigenous women; state regulation of women's dress is opposed.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Indigenous peoples across borders are linked, but this is not stated as a goal for political union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Kuokkanen supports self-governing Indigenous institutions, but she claims land and inherent self-government, which goes beyond cultural autonomy alone.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources discuss peoples with homelands, not persecuted minorities choosing between emigration and local rights struggles.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The sources attribute change to colonisation and resistance, not to a theory of material determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is not discussed in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Kuokkanen and Smith critique settler majorities' control over Indigenous peoples; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Kuokkanen argues governance institutions must be gendered and women's views included; parity as a quota is inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic empires are not discussed; the movement's anti-imperial stance rejects the colonial element but the sources are silent on trade blocs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; communal ethics of responsibility resemble the idea but no source links them.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Guevarist foco theory is not discussed; the Zapatista armed uprising is mentioned in Wikipedia, but its lessons on this question are not stated.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed; some Indigenous systems have hereditary roles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement criticises settler-centred historical narratives and wants Indigenous history included; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Missionary and state civilising policies are the colonial wrongs the movement opposes.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; redress of historic injustice is supported.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform proposals are not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism can avoid collapse is not discussed in the sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory delinking is not discussed; the sources criticise neoliberal integration but propose no break with trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist theory about workers in rich countries that the sources do not address.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Discrimination against Indigenous women is a central harm; the movement opposes it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: NWAC-style advocacy sought constitutionally entrenched sex equality in self-government, per Kuokkanen's emphasis on gendering governance; a general bill of rights is inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Adherents emphasise honouring treaties as nation-to-nation agreements while rejecting colonial impositions; border-dividing treaties are not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; Indigenous governance includes hereditary and clan-based leadership that adherents would defend while demanding women's inclusion.

minority-veto.rationale: Smith's consensus-oriented, relational governance resonates, but no source endorses individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to illegitimate domination is central to Smith's account, though ruler-constitution language is foreign to it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Kuokkanen critiques settler-state sovereignty, so parliamentary supremacy over Indigenous nations is not endorsed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Relational ethics extend responsibility to non-human beings; animal suffering is not explicitly discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Hunting and use with respect and reciprocity are accepted in Indigenous traditions; inferred from reciprocal responsibility to non-humans.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not addressed; adherents emphasise collective responsibility, not paternalistic duty of elites.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Indigenous feminism is activist and politically engaged (Idle No More, MMIW organising).

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream media is criticised for neglecting MMIW, but no general theory of pacification.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Colonial extraction of land and labour is central, but world-systems theory is not named.

native-born-offices.rationale: Smith rejects nation-state nativism and exclusionary nationalism; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; self-determination is valued but not tied to rejecting aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Land return from settler states is central, but this statement concerns interstate war losses.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources argue for Indigenous self-government within and alongside settler states, not Indigenous rule over settlers; rejecting the statement is an inference.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Smith's anti-domination politics suggests support; not discussed.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject apologetic settler-nation narratives.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Colonial commemoration is contested by decolonial movements; not discussed directly.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Kuokkanen centres women's structural disadvantage; men's disadvantage is not addressed, though colonial harm to Indigenous men is acknowledged in the field.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Smith says Native women are most likely to be killed by domestic violence and insists the issue is not secondary; symmetry is not asserted.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Smith and Kuokkanen seek Indigenous models of governance rather than imposed Western forms, though they also reject using culture to justify patriarchy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Anti-domination politics opposes military political rule; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wikipedia notes colonial division of public and private labour undermined women's authority; recognising care labour is a plausible implication.

filial-duty.rationale: Responsibility-based kinship ethics (Kim Anderson) emphasise obligations across generations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; Indigenous land control concerns differ from strategic industry.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Women's autonomy within marriage is valued, and colonial marriage law was imposed; divorce law is not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Participatory, accountable governance fits, but nothing specific in sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Smith ties sovereignty to connection to the earth and Wikipedia describes land as communal responsibility rather than individual property.

single-official-language.rationale: Colonial language suppression is part of the cultural losses Starblanket and Green name; revival of Indigenous languages is supported.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; all settler ownership is contested in principle.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Intersectional analysis treats unequal outcomes as evidence of structural discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Reciprocal relation to land stands against consumption culture; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Smith links patriarchy to empire; opposition to imperial intervention inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Capitalist restructuring and extractive industry are criticised in Wikipedia's account.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Indigenous organisations often rely on outside funds; not discussed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Wikipedia documents state control of Indigenous reproduction; pronatalist state engineering is likely distrusted.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Barriers to employment are named as part of marginalisation; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; Smith distrusts the democratic nation-state's record.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Smith rejects state legitimacy over Indigenous peoples but not law generally.

non-intervention.rationale: Absolute non-intervention is not discussed; Smith opposes imperial intervention but the sources do not state an absolute rule.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy scapegoating of minorities contradicts anti-domination ethics.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Smith critiques the heteronormative state, but abolition of state marriage is not stated.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The inquiry stresses truth-gathering and accountability.

local-production.rationale: Food sovereignty and land-based economies are prized; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Smith's models of relational organising partially fit but the sources do not endorse informal groups over formal ones.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Kuokkanen critiques settler-state sovereignty and Indigenous activists invoke international law against national law.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Imperial domination is the opposite of the interrelated sovereignty Smith describes.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Indigenous self-government debates include fiscal autonomy but sources do not settle it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The sources do not take up the possessions versus means of production distinction.

defeat-communism.rationale: The sources do not discuss anti-communism; the movement is not defined by it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service-delivery models are not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Spirituality is integral to many Indigenous worldviews, though missionary Christianity is criticised.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Capitalism is presented as a colonial imposition that disrupted women's economic authority.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Wikipedia says capitalism and gendered labour divisions disrupted women's authority, and sees decolonisation as essential to gender justice.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; community kinship care is valued but not specifically as public service.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; language revival is supported but not purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Kuokkanen speaks of treaty negotiations as sites where Indigenous self-determination must be gendered, implying treaties are binding nation-to-nation agreements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Smith's vision of non-hierarchical, relational communities fits; no explicit endorsement of cooperatives.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement of minority regions by a majority is colonisation, which is the movement's core target.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Not stated; Smith emphasises alternatives to domination but not this framing.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Kuokkanen says land is at the heart of Indigenous feminist theory and Starblanket and Green stress histories of land theft.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denying documented genocide conflicts with the movement's insistence on recognising genocide.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Smith criticises heteronormative nationalism, and the inquiry includes 2SLGBTQQIA people among victims.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; religious coercion linked to colonial missionaries.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonialism as extraction and subordination is the central object of critique in Wikipedia's account.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine on which this ideology has no stated position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A question of Islamist politics that the sources do not address.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Kuokkanen argues for explicit inclusion of women's voices in community decisions and governance.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Wikipedia defines Indigenous feminism as an intersectional theory building on Crenshaw.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The inquiry names 2SLGBTQQIA people as victims needing protection, and Smith opposes heteronormative nationalism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; movement is firmly aligned with anticolonial left politics.

alienated-labor.rationale: Wikipedia describes colonial gendered labour breaking Indigenous economic life; alienation language is not used.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority is grounded in relationships and land, not divine delegation; Smith critiques the Christian Right.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; cultural dress is typically defended as Indigenous expression.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Silencing of survivors would be opposed; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mixed-economy models are not discussed; the sources critique capitalism's colonial roots without proposing a market model.

rich-first.rationale: Unequal development is attributed to colonial extraction.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary leadership exists in some Indigenous systems but not addressed here.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is not discussed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Neoliberal restructuring is criticised in Wikipedia's Oaxaca discussion.

property-franchise.rationale: Wikipedia notes that voting-rights exclusions barred Indigenous women, so restricting votes is opposed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Wikipedia treats colonial treatment of women and land together, and Kuokkanen notes colonialism treats Indigenous female bodies as it treats the land.

reification.rationale: Lukacsian theory is not discussed; the sources use colonialism and heteropatriarchy as their critical concepts.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mainstream media neglect of MMIW is criticised, but the specific claim is not addressed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law theory is not discussed in the sources.

racial-franchise.rationale: Exclusion from the vote is documented as part of colonial oppression of Aboriginal women.

online-participation.rationale: Digital democracy is not discussed in the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Public truth-telling and accountability are central to the inquiry.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Colonial regulation of marriage is criticised.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with participatory themes but unsupported.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Critique of capitalism implies concern; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Smith is critical of militarism and so adherents are split on whether inclusion in the military is a goal.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Indigenous spiritual practice is valued and attacks on religion would be seen as coercive.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Many scholars-activists in the field favour abolition, but the sources do not state it for the movement as a whole.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational design is not discussed; Kuokkanen's work concerns inclusion of women in Indigenous governance, not power sharing between communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Poverty and structural neglect are state-responsibility issues; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction-risk policy is not discussed; the movement's priorities are decolonisation and ending violence against women.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Wikipedia notes heteropatriarchal traditions excluded women and two-spirit people from leadership, which adherents oppose.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Colonial patriarchal marriage norms are criticised, so equal authority is supported.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not discussed; the sources neither endorse nor oppose votes for resident non-citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Housing insecurity is cited as a harm; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Indigenous cultural property is a live concern, but abolition is not addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Militarised nationalist training conflicts with Smith's critique of nationalism.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The inquiry concluded that laws and institutions perpetuate violations amounting to genocide, and Wikipedia calls the MMIW crisis ongoing genocide.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; Smith opposes domestic violence and defence of the vulnerable is not condemned.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; critique of nationalist myths vs Indigenous continuity claims.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Intersectionality and attention to two-spirit people suggest wariness of a single category of women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; MMIW victims are commemorated but not as martyrs of a nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics as a struggle of good and evil is not a framing used in the sources, though spirituality matters in Indigenous traditions.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A debate within diaspora nationalism that the sources do not address.

culture-before-state.rationale: Smith separates liberation from state-building, and Wikipedia stresses cultural renewal, but sequence is not stated.

god-not-male.rationale: Heteropatriarchal religion is criticised; Indigenous spiritualities often include female and non-gendered figures; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is not discussed in the sources; Wikipedia notes heteropatriarchal religious traditions that excluded women, but offers no test for scripture.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Opposed to domination by a majority at the expense of minorities.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Territorial self-government for a people fits Indigenous self-determination.

independent-unions.rationale: Anti-hierarchy and independence from the state; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A debate within socialism that the sources do not address.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Barriers to services are named as harms; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not discussed in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Community and communal ownership suit Indigenous land practice; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Smith praises models of nationhood built on interrelatedness and responsibility, rather than domination; inferred as confederal.

family-wage.rationale: Wikipedia notes the colonial public/private labour split; a male-breadwinner family wage is not endorsed.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Life-extension research is not discussed in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payment privacy is not discussed in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is not discussed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Individual is balanced with collective in the sources.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Indigenous spiritual relations are valued in Wikipedia's account.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Kuokkanen holds Indigenous self-determination is inherent, not a power delegated by the settler state; revocable powers would deny it.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; reciprocal land relations suggest caution.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form is not discussed; land-based ethics might favour limited footprint but the sources do not say.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Not addressed; Indigenous peoples organise as peoples but racial blocs are a different claim.

racial-pride.rationale: Cultural pride and resurgence are supported; stated for Indigenous identity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not discussed; Smith links militarism to empire but the sources do not state a doctrine on wars.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Language-based nationhood is not discussed; Indigenous language revival is, but not as a definition of the nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Religious electorates are not discussed in the sources.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed; the movement criticises nationalist conspiracy.

free-public-college.rationale: Barriers to education are named as harms; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Wikipedia describes Indigenous environmental care as reciprocal responsibility; Smith mentions past, present and future being copresent in ceremony.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; adherents warn against essentialising, though some emphasise women's relational roles.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret treaties are not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital flow regulation is not discussed in the sources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The sources do not discuss who may bear arms; Indigenous self-defence claims and distrust of police pull against a state monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Refusal of orders is not discussed in the sources.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credit design is not discussed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; poverty concerns suggest against austerity rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Smith calls for challenging the nation-state itself, yet many adherents work through its institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Distinct Indigenous models of governance and economy are valued.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Wikipedia describes land as relation and responsibility rather than commodity capital.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Settler colonialism within states is the central frame, extended internally.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Human nature is not discussed; the sources are wary of universals imposed by colonisers but defend human rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Mainstream media neglect of MMIW is criticised; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Perennialism is not discussed in the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural price policy is not discussed in the sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: Class-based party formation is not discussed in the sources.

ban-fgm.rationale: Opposition to violence against women is central; this specific practice is not discussed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Wikipedia covers the Indian Act's loss of women's status and property and restoring women's economic authority is a goal.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic dispute about naming that the sources do not address.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Kuokkanen would insist women be included in any customary governance, so split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Reciprocal responsibility to land takes priority; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Linguistic assimilation echoes colonial policy; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union security rules are not discussed in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Wikipedia records historic exclusion of Indigenous women from the vote; ID barriers are inferred as concerning.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Kuokkanen wants substantive inclusion, not only electoral procedure.

premarital-sex.rationale: Colonial authorities enforced modesty and monogamy norms; adherents reject them.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is not discussed; poverty relief is valued but not this mechanism.

women-suffrage.rationale: Wikipedia notes Aboriginal women in Canada were denied the vote until the 1960s and criticises this exclusion.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Wikipedia says heteropatriarchal religious traditions excluded women and missionaries enforced colonial norms, but Indigenous spirituality is valued, so adherents split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Racialisation is treated as a colonial process; not stated directly.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The inquiry calls on governments for transformative institutional change, and NWAC-style advocacy seeks gender impact analysis of laws.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Kuokkanen argues treaties and self-government must be gendered from their initiation rather than adding women afterwards.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its view of land as relation and responsibility, in opposition to colonial property regimes.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperial critique and focus on accountability for violence; sources do not discuss international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from its decolonial critique of imposed Christianity and respect for Indigenous spiritual plurality.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from Smith's call for non-hierarchical governance beyond the state, and its critique of bureaucratic states.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from Smith's preference for non-hierarchical, community-based governance over layered representation.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from its analysis of colonialism and imposed patriarchy, in which churches were instruments of colonisation.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Self-determination and Indigenous governance over land are central to Kuokkanen's argument, which includes territorial self-government.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on self-determination of peoples; no source discusses plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from Smith's view that sovereignty should go beyond the nation-state and colonial boundaries.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from its critique of capitalism and consumption and emphasis on relation to land.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its priority on land and self-determination, which implies control over outside settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its critique of empire and militarism; it would favour neither, and equal treatment otherwise.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Indigenous feminism treats land as a source of relation, responsibility and identity, and puts land and decolonisation at the centre of gender justice.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The inquiry and Smith's work centre state and colonial violence against Indigenous people and opposition to policing harms, so killing without trial is rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: The sources never address foreign alignment; anti-imperial commitments cut against both great powers, so neutral is inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Indigenous feminism focuses on self-determination within settler states, not on a state protecting kin abroad, so neutral is inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Relational views of land as shared and held in trust fit with compensation for appropriation; this is inferred from anticolonial and anti-capitalist commitments.

self-ownership.rationale: Indigenous feminists prefer relation and responsibility to Western liberal individualism, but they also demand bodily autonomy for women, so adherents are split.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources give no tax position; regressive taxes might be disliked but this is not addressed.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The inquiry demands specific services for Indigenous women but also broad structural change, and the sources do not frame it as universal versus targeted.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Collectivist and community-based governance prefers organised collectives and relations rather than leader-centred rule; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anti-capitalist and anticolonial commitments suggest opposition to corporate privilege, though this is inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Indigenous spiritual traditions are valued but are not denominations, and adherents differ.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Emphasis on Indigenous knowledge and traditions alongside modern self-government suggests combining both; this is inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The movement opposes imposed patriarchy and subordination of women, so women's equal right to leave a marriage follows directly.

national-resource-control.rationale: Indigenous self-determination includes control over lands and resources and opposes foreign extraction, though the statement's national framing is inferred.

missingStatements.text: Indigenous self-government arrangements should guarantee women's participation and gender equality from the outset.
missingStatements.rationale: Kuokkanen argues treaties and self-government must be gendered from their initiation rather than adding women afterwards.

missingStatements.text: Violence against the women of a colonised people is a tool of colonial domination, not only a crime between individuals.
missingStatements.rationale: The inquiry traces violence to colonial and patriarchal policies and Kuokkanen says colonialism treats Indigenous women's bodies like the land.
missingStatements.declined: Framing is analytical and loaded rather than a policy position other ideologies can answer neutrally.

notes: Some Indigenous women reject the feminist label as Western, and others hold that feminism has much to offer; positions on sex work, abolition and the role of the state are contested. Andrea Smith's scholarly identity has been disputed, so her essay is cited only for the sovereignty arguments it states.
